title: 2003 AMC 10B Problem 3
statement: The sum of \(5\) consecutive even integers is \(4\) less than the sum of the first \(8\) consecutive odd counting numbers. What is the smallest of the even integers?

solutions.text:
The first \(8\) odd counting numbers sum to \(1+3+\cdots+15=64.\)

Letting \(n\) be the smallest even integer, \[ \begin{gathered} n+(n+2)+(n+4) \\ {}+(n+6)+(n+8) \\ = 5n+20 = 60, \end{gathered} \] so \(n=8.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The first \(8\) odd counting numbers sum to \(8^2\)
Write the even integers as \(n,\) \(n+2,\) \(n+4,\) \(n+6,\) \(n+8\) and set their sum equal to \(64-4\)
